title: Understanding Variance
text: To find the standard deviation, we first need to calculate the variance. Remember, variance is the expectation of the squared deviation of a random variable from its mean. Can you think about how to calculate the variance for a single customer and then extend it to $$10$$ customers?

title: Calculating Variance for One Customer
text: For one customer, the variance of the purchase value can be calculated using the formula: variance $$=$$ $$E\left(X^2\right)$$ - $${E\left(X\right)}^2$$. Try to find E(X) and $$E\left(X^2\right)$$ for a single customer.

title: Expected Value for One Customer
text: The expected value E(X) for one customer is the sum of the products of each item's price and its probability of being purchased. Can you calculate this value?

title: Expected Value of Squared Purchases
text: To find $$E\left(X^2\right)$$, consider the square of the purchase value for each possible outcome and multiply it by its probability. What are the possible purchase values and their probabilities?

title: Variance for $$10$$ Customers
text: Once you have the variance for one customer, how would you calculate the variance for $$10$$ customers?

title: Standard Deviation from Variance
text: Remember, the standard deviation is the square root of the variance. Once you have the variance for $$10$$ customers, how can you find the standard deviation?
